subject: Mythology
title: Fairy Mounds and the Sidhe
description: A micro-lesson that makes Fairy Mounds and the Sidhe usable.

hook.text: Across Ireland, ancient burial mounds were feared as entrances to a hidden world ruled by powerful fairy beings.

buildup.text: The Sidhe were not cute pixies. They were the ancient gods of Ireland, tall, beautiful, and dangerously powerful.

discovery.text: Disturbing a fairy mound was believed to bring terrible misfortune, illness, or even death to the offender.

twist.text: In modern Ireland, construction projects have been rerouted to avoid destroying fairy mounds that locals revere.

climax.text: The belief in the Sidhe survived Christianity, colonization, and modernization — lasting over two thousand years.

punchline.text: Ireland paves roads around hills that fairies might still live in.

quiz.question: Who were the Sidhe in Celtic mythology?
options: Tiny winged creatures who lived in flowers
Ancient gods who retreated into fairy mounds
Human druids who gained magical powers
